description: We're a team of technology enthusiasts interested in web development, AI, data science, IoT, and space science. We enjoy solving real-world problems and turning ideas into working solutions. We're looking for curious and collaborative people with skills in frontend/backend development, Python, AI/ML, UI/UX, GIS, remote sensing, or scientific research. Most importantly, we value creativity, teamwork, and a willingness to learn. All experience levels are welcome!
summary: AgriClimate is an agricultural intelligence platform that uses NASA satellite data and environmental information to help farmers and agricultural officers make better-informed decisions. It brings together insights on crop health, soil moisture, rainfall, and changing weather conditions through an interactive dashboard and GIS-based monitoring system. The platform also provides crop suitability analysis, irrigation guidance, and early warnings for potential droughts, floods, and fires. By turning complex Earth observation data into information that is easier to understand and act on, AgriClimate aims to help farmers identify risks earlier, manage agricultural resources more effectively, and make informed decisions about their crops. We developed it with a particular focus on agricultural challenges in Bangladesh, where unpredictable weather and climate-related risks can have a significant impact on farming communities.
details:
AgriClimate is a satellite-powered agricultural intelligence platform designed to help farmers and agricultural extension officers make informed decisions using Earth observation data. We developed it with a particular focus on agricultural challenges in Bangladesh, where unpredictable rainfall, flooding, drought, and changing climate conditions can directly affect farming communities.

The platform brings together environmental data from NASA missions and makes it accessible through two dedicated interfaces: a Farmer View and an Officer Control Panel. While farmers receive practical information and recommendations, agricultural officers can monitor conditions across different areas, review resource requests, and coordinate responses through an interactive GIS-based dashboard.

Some of the key features include:

  • Climate and Crop Monitoring: Displays weather conditions, rainfall patterns, soil moisture, vegetation health, and crop stress using satellite-derived indicators such as NDVI.
  • Crop Calendar: Provides recommended sowing windows, crop growth timelines, seasonal irrigation schedules, and estimated harvesting periods based on historical climate data.
  • Crop Recommendations: Evaluates soil moisture, temperature, rainfall, solar radiation, and vegetation conditions to identify crops that may be suitable for a particular area.
  • Smart Irrigation Guidance: Uses soil moisture and crop water stress information to help estimate irrigation requirements and determine where water resources are needed most.
  • Solar Pump Transfer Requests: Allows farmers to request the transfer of available solar irrigation pumps when their fields face water shortages. Agricultural officers can review these requests and coordinate pump allocation based on local irrigation priorities.
  • Drought and Flood Alerts: Combines rainfall, soil moisture, and terrain information to identify areas potentially vulnerable to drought, flooding, and waterlogging.
  • Fire and Crop Risk Monitoring: Uses NASA FIRMS satellite observations to identify thermal anomalies and potential agricultural fire incidents.
  • Crop Input Advisory: Provides guidance on potential crop nutrient deficiencies and suitable soil or fertilizer interventions based on vegetation and environmental indicators.

For agricultural officers, the platform provides an interactive GIS command center with multiple satellite-data layers, block-level environmental statistics, monitoring tools, alert management, and resource coordination features. This makes it easier to identify vulnerable areas and understand where assistance may be needed.

AgriClimate integrates several NASA datasets, including MODIS, Landsat 8/9, SMAP, GPM IMERG, NASA POWER, FIRMS, and SRTM. Each contributes a different perspective on agricultural conditions, from vegetation health and soil moisture to precipitation, temperature, fire activity, and terrain. We combine these observations using geospatial processing, environmental indices, and rule-based scoring to turn raw data into understandable agricultural insights.

Our initial implementation focuses on 12 administrative monitoring blocks in Kurigram, Bangladesh. We chose a localized approach because conditions can vary significantly between nearby agricultural areas, and broad regional weather information does not always provide enough detail for individual farming decisions.

The platform was developed using Next.js, React, TypeScript, and Tailwind CSS, with MapLibre GL JS for geospatial visualization, Zustand for state management, and TanStack Query for data management. Python and TypeScript are also used in the data processing and ingestion workflows. The application supports both English and Bengali to make its information more accessible to local users.

What makes AgriClimate different is its focus on connecting environmental monitoring with practical action. Rather than stopping at showing a farmer that their area is experiencing low soil moisture, the platform connects that information to irrigation guidance, pump transfer requests, and resource prioritization. Similarly, crop and climate information is brought together through the crop calendar and recommendation system to support planning throughout the growing season.

Throughout development, we considered the different needs of farmers and agricultural officers, accessibility, language, data availability, satellite resolution, environmental variability, and the practical limitations of rural connectivity.

Our aim is to make satellite-based environmental information more useful at the local level, helping farming communities prepare for changing conditions, manage limited resources more effectively, and make better-informed decisions throughout the agricultural cycle.
